that down time can also cost them crops, granted most have insurance on them. It just ends up costing us more money to buy produce, and the wait time for a mechanic could be days in peak times.

I just wanted to add on to your post.

There is almost never an increase to the cost of produce. The farmer can only sell his produce at a certain price unless he is selling directly to the consumer himself. He takes the monetary hit straight to the teeth.

A lot of farmers don't have insurance and even if they did, this would not be covered. Insurance covers your crops if they are destroyed by natural means. If you don't have the equipment to harvest, tough luck. If you needed the tractor to spray and since you didn't you lose half the crop to blight, insurance would cover the planting costs of exactly the yield you lost.

So let's say you have 100 acres of corn. It costs 100$/acre (labour seed sprays) to plant the corn. You can then sell it at $500/acre. Now insurance comes around and they say "hey half this corn is harvestable, so we will only pay you for 50 acres". You get 50100$= 5000$ not 50500$ = 25,000$.
This is the new consumer future. You rent the things you thought you previously owned.

As a former farmer ( and tractor dealer ) the government demands of more fuel efficient and cleaner running engines is what is driving the increased use of electronics in farm equipment. Savings in consumption is often derailed by the need to call in the dealership - sometimes from hours away to do repairs plus the high cost of proprietary parts increases costs substantially. It's "great" when the tractor is under warranty because the only thing that it costs you is your downtime, right? If a combine goes down the farmer still has to pay the operator and the ancillary people that he needs to keep the machine efficiently. Plus, depending on the crop, processors sometimes are very specific regarding delivery times and if you miss your scheduled delivery time they pencil you in for "later".

One nice thing is that for well maintained tractors which don't have all the electronics, the used market is very hot .
